chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Sidemen who came through his bands: Parlan, Waldron, Knepper, Shaw
summary: Johnson asks about players who benefited from his bands; Clarence Shaw's death and writing.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What about some of the people who -- it's been said, and I think it's accurate, that the bands that you've had have really been the making of a lot of players. They've learned, it's like their college education. And a number of them have gone on to do very, very well, and a lot of them who seemed very promising never again played as well as they did play with they played with you. And I just wonder if you wanted to talk about some of the people that you had special good feelings about, who came through your bands?
Yeah, Horace Parlan, Mal Waldron, Horse Porlong, Mel Waldren, Knepper Jimmy Nipper, Clarence Shaw, Bookee Ervin.
Clarence Shaw, did anybody find him?
No, he's dead. He's been dead quite a while.
He was in Detroit part of Chicago, I forgot which. We were out there, he invited us to dinner a couple of times to his house. He was rehearsing some music. He was a very fine writer.
I never heard anything he wrote, but he was a lovely player. The Tijuana album is one of the reasons it's so good is that he played so well on it.
He's a very tasty player. In my bands,
